h: Seeds, valleys and the Sussex countryside
p: The Millennium Seed Bank is one of the things that makes Wakehurst so special. It's a vital conservation project, storing seeds from tens of thousands of plant species to protect them from extinction. Visitors can look through windows into the labs and learn how the seeds are collected and stored. It's a fascinating peek into how science is helping to safeguard the world's plants.

The Elizabethan mansion, built in 1590, is the grand centrepiece, and the gardens around it are full of colour. Then head out into the wider landscape. The Westwood Valley and the Himalayan Glade are full of plants from around the world, while the Loder Valley Nature Reserve is a quieter, wilder spot for spotting birds and wildlife.

Allow at least half a day, more if you're a keen walker. Some of the paths are steep, especially in the valleys, so wear sturdy shoes. Winter brings its own magic, with festive events and light trails in recent years.

Nearby, the village of Ardingly is home to the South of England Showground and Ardingly Reservoir, a lovely spot for a waterside walk. Garden lovers are spoilt for choice in this corner of Sussex, with Nymans and Borde Hill Garden both a short drive away. Train fans can head over to the Bluebell Railway, a heritage steam line running between Sheffield Park and East Grinstead.
